tests.title: Both variables are read through GetVariable after the lock is taken and before any fetch, on every sync
given: a recording GetVariable stub, a recording lock and recording fetch stubs
PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE initially unset
tests.when: two syncs run, with PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE set to origin between them, without rebuilding the handler or config
then: GetVariable("workspace", slug, "PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE") and PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY are called once per sync
the recorded order is lock, variable reads, first fetch
the first sync performs no origin fetch and the second performs one
tests.pseudocode: run(sync); setVar(origin); run(sync); assert calls[0:3]==[lock,getvar,getvar] ; assert originFetches==[0,1]

tests.title: The exact value origin selects origin as the patch authority
given: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE is "origin"
tests.when: a carry-patch sync runs with counting fetch stubs
then: the origin fetch stub is called once
the response has origin_fetched true
tests.pseudocode: setVar('PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE','origin'); r=sync(); assert originFetch.count==1; assert r.origin_fetched==true

tests.title: Unset, error, hub, Origin, empty and other values select hub without an error
given: a table of PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE states: unset, lookup error, "hub", "Origin", "ORIGIN", "", "garbage"
tests.when: a sync runs for each row
then: every sync answers HTTP 200
no origin fetch and no origin credential lookup happens
origin_fetched is false and no patches_synced field is present
tests.pseudocode: for v in rows: r=sync(v); assert r.status==200; assert originFetch.count==0; assert r.origin_fetched==false; assert 'patches_synced' not in r

tests.title: The exact value report applies the report policy to a diverged branch
given: origin mode with one diverged candidate patch
PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY is "report"
then: the local branch is unchanged
the element has state diverged and action none
tests.pseudocode: setVar(policy,'report'); r=sync(); assert r.patches_synced[0].state=='diverged'; assert refLocal==oldTip

tests.title: Unset, error, replace, Report and other policy values apply replace without an error
given: origin mode with one diverged candidate patch
a table of PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY states: unset, lookup error, "replace", "Report", "", "x"
tests.when: a sync runs for each row
then: every sync answers HTTP 200
the element has action replaced
patches_diverged is []
tests.pseudocode: for v in rows: r=sync(v); assert r.status==200; assert r.patches_synced[0].action=='replaced'; assert r.patches_diverged==[]

tests.title: In hub mode the divergence policy is ignored
given: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE unset
PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY is "report" in one run and "replace" in another
a patch branch that differs from the fork
tests.when: a sync runs in each configuration
then: both responses are identical
no patch ref and no refs/hub/replaced/* ref is written
tests.pseudocode: assert sync(policy='report')==sync(policy='replace'); assert refsWritten==[]

tests.title: The origin fetch brings in fork branches with the heads refspec, no tags, and treats up-to-date as success
given: a real bare fork with branches and a tag, a trunk cloned from it with origin pointing at the fork, and no GIT_PAT set (credentials resolve to none)
tests.when: the production FetchOrigin is called twice
then: refs/remotes/origin/<branch> equals the fork tip for every branch
no tag is created in the trunk
the second call returns nil (already up to date)
tests.pseudocode: FetchOrigin(ctx, trunk, auth); assert rev-parse origin/b==forkTip; assert tags(trunk)==[]; assert FetchOrigin(...)==nil

tests.title: Origin credentials follow GIT_PAT, then GIT_USERNAME/GIT_PASSWORD, then none
given: a secrets store with three configurations: GIT_PAT set; only GIT_USERNAME and GIT_PASSWORD set; neither set
tests.when: the wired ResolveOriginAuth is called for each configuration
then: it returns the same auth value as workspace.ResolveCloneAuth in each case
tests.pseudocode: for cfg in cfgs: assert ResolveOriginAuth(store,slug)==workspace.ResolveCloneAuth(store,slug)

tests.title: Sync steps run in the documented order under the held lock
given: origin mode with a call-recording stub for every step and for the lock
then: the recorded order is lock, origin credential resolution, upstream fetch, origin fetch, upstream-base resolution, patch refresh, merge detection, workspace update
the lock is held until after the workspace update
tests.pseudocode: assert calls==[lock,resolveOriginAuth,fetchUpstream,fetchOrigin,resolveBase,refresh,detect,updateWs,unlock]

tests.title: A credential-resolution failure answers 502 before any fetch and changes nothing
given: origin mode, ResolveOriginAuth returns an error
upstream_head_sha, last_sync_at, patch rows and refs snapshotted
then: the status is 502 with message "failed to resolve origin credentials"
neither the upstream nor the origin fetch stub was called
upstream_head_sha, last_sync_at, patch rows and refs equal the snapshot
tests.pseudocode: r=sync(); assert r.status==502; assert r.error=='failed to resolve origin credentials'; assert fetches==0; assert snapshot()==before

tests.title: An origin fetch failure after a successful upstream fetch answers 502 origin_fetch_failed and changes nothing
given: origin mode with upstream advanced, FetchOrigin returning an error
snapshot of upstream_head_sha, last_sync_at, patch statuses, persisted origin sync columns and refs/heads/*
then: the status is 502, message "origin fetch failed", error_type "origin_fetch_failed"
the upstream fetch stub was called once
the snapshot is unchanged
no rebuild job is enqueued
tests.pseudocode: r=sync(); assert r.status==502; assert r.error_type=='origin_fetch_failed'; assert snapshot()==before; assert jobs==0

tests.title: The hub source performs zero origin fetches and zero origin credential lookups
given: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE unset, counting stubs for FetchOrigin and ResolveOriginAuth
tests.when: a sync runs, with and without an upstream advance
then: FetchOrigin count is 0
ResolveOriginAuth count is 0
tests.pseudocode: sync(); assert fetchOrigin.n==0 and resolveOriginAuth.n==0

tests.title: Origin mode with a nil FetchOrigin answers 500 origin fetch is not configured
given: origin mode, SyncAPIConfig.FetchOrigin is nil
state snapshot
then: the status is 500 with message "origin fetch is not configured"
the snapshot is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: cfg.FetchOrigin=nil; r=sync(); assert r.status==500; assert r.error=='origin fetch is not configured'; assert snapshot()==before

tests.title: A branch deleted on a real bare fork loses its tracking ref after an origin-mode sync
given: a real bare fork and real upstream, trunk with refs/remotes/origin/feat from an earlier fetch
feat is registered as an active patch
feat is then deleted on the fork
tests.when: an origin-mode sync runs through the production fetch
then: refs/remotes/origin/feat no longer exists
the element for feat has state missing_on_origin
tests.pseudocode: git(fork,'branch -D feat'); r=sync(); assert not refExists(trunk,'refs/remotes/origin/feat'); assert r.patches_synced[0].state=='missing_on_origin'

tests.title: Only active, conflict and disabled patches are candidates, in position order, excluding the integration branch
given: real fork and upstream
patches in positions 1-6 with statuses active, conflict, disabled, merged_upstream, deleted, and one active patch named like the integration branch
then: patches_synced lists exactly the active, conflict and disabled branches in position order
the merged_upstream, deleted and integration-named patches have no element and their refs are untouched
tests.pseudocode: r=sync(); assert names(r.patches_synced)==['a','c','d']

tests.title: A branch missing on the fork is reported missing_on_origin and left alone
given: real fork without branch feat, local refs/heads/feat exists, patch status active
then: the element has state missing_on_origin, action none, no origin_sha, local_sha set
refs/heads/feat is unchanged
the patch status is still active
the persisted origin_sync_state is missing_on_origin and origin_sha is null
tests.pseudocode: r=sync(); e=r.patches_synced[0]; assert e.state=='missing_on_origin' and e.action=='none'; assert 'origin_sha' not in e; assert status=='active'

tests.title: A missing local branch is created at the fork tip
given: real fork with branch feat, no refs/heads/feat in the trunk, patch active
then: refs/heads/feat equals the fork tip
the element has action created, state in_sync, local_sha and origin_sha equal to the fork tip
the persisted state is in_sync with origin_sha set
tests.pseudocode: r=sync(); assert rev(trunk,'refs/heads/feat')==forkTip; assert e.action=='created' and e.state=='in_sync'

tests.title: Equal tips write no ref and report in_sync
given: real fork and trunk where refs/heads/feat equals refs/remotes/origin/feat
tests.when: an origin-mode sync runs with a ref-write recorder wrapping the git runner
then: no update-ref call is made for feat
the element has action none, state in_sync
the persisted state is in_sync
tests.pseudocode: r=sync(); assert updateRefCalls==[]; assert e.action=='none' and e.state=='in_sync'

tests.title: A local tip that is a strict ancestor of the fork tip is fast-forwarded
given: real fork where feat is two commits ahead of the hub's refs/heads/feat
then: refs/heads/feat equals the fork tip
the element has action fast_forwarded, state in_sync, replaced_sha absent
no refs/hub/replaced/feat exists
tests.pseudocode: r=sync(); assert rev(local)==forkTip; assert e.action=='fast_forwarded'; assert not refExists('refs/hub/replaced/feat')

tests.title: Divergence under replace backs up the old tip and moves the branch to the fork tip
given: real fork and trunk where feat diverged (a hub commit and a different fork commit on a common base)
policy replace
then: refs/hub/replaced/feat holds the former local tip
refs/heads/feat holds the fork tip
the element has action replaced, state in_sync, replaced_sha equal to the old local tip
a pre-existing older backup for feat is overwritten
tests.pseudocode: old=rev(local); r=sync(); assert rev('refs/hub/replaced/feat')==old; assert rev(local)==forkTip; assert e.replaced_sha==old

tests.title: Divergence under report leaves the local branch and reports both SHAs
given: real fork and trunk with a diverged feat
policy report
then: refs/heads/feat is unchanged
no refs/hub/replaced/feat exists
the element has state diverged, action none, local_sha and origin_sha set and different
patches_diverged equals ["feat"]
the persisted state is diverged
tests.pseudocode: r=sync(); assert rev(local)==old; assert e.state=='diverged'; assert r.patches_diverged==['feat']

tests.title: A fork tip that is a strict ancestor of the local tip is divergence and follows the policy
given: real fork whose feat is behind the hub's refs/heads/feat (hub has extra commits)
tests.when: a sync runs once under replace and once, on a fresh copy, under report
then: under replace the backup holds the longer hub tip, the local ref equals the fork tip and the action is replaced
under report the local ref is unchanged and the state is diverged
tests.pseudocode: assert isAncestor(forkTip, localTip) and forkTip!=localTip; run both policies; check refs

tests.title: For any pair of local and fork histories exactly the first matching rule applies, decided on SHAs
given: a real git repository with generated commit graphs and a recording GitRunner
tests.when: for any candidate whose fork branch is present or absent, local branch present or absent, and tips equal, ancestor, descendant or unrelated
then: the outcome equals the first matching rule in the order fork missing, local missing, same commit, local strict ancestor, diverged
every IsAncestor call receives 40-hex SHAs and never branch names
exactly one rule's ref writes occur
tests.pseudocode: for (fork,local,rel) in gen(): out=refresh(c); assert out==expected(first_match(rel)); assert all(isSha(a) for a in isAncestorArgs)

tests.title: Every patch and backup ref is written with update-ref carrying the expected old SHA, never checkout, reset or branch -f
given: a recording GitRunner over a real repo with one created, one fast-forwarded and one replaced candidate
then: each ref write is update-ref <ref> <new> <expected-old> through Run
the create uses the all-zero SHA as expected-old
the others use the tip resolved at the start of that step
no checkout, reset or branch -f call appears (apart from the HardReset of 20-REQ-4.2)
tests.pseudocode: calls=recorder.calls; assert all(c[0]=='update-ref' for c in writes); assert createCall[-1]=='0'*40; assert no c[0] in ['checkout','branch']

tests.title: Moving the checked-out branch hard-resets the working tree to the new tip
given: real trunk whose HEAD is refs/heads/feat with a clean working tree
the fork has a new commit on feat adding a file
then: the new file exists in the trunk working directory
git status is clean
moving a branch that is not HEAD performs no hard reset
tests.pseudocode: r=sync(); assert fileExists(trunk,'new.txt'); assert status(trunk)==''

tests.title: A lost compare-and-swap persists earlier outcomes, stops the refresh and returns 500
given: real fork, three candidates a, b, c where a is fast-forwardable
a hub push to b lands after the ancestry check, simulated with a runner hook that advances refs/heads/b just before update-ref
AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC unset
then: the status is 500 with message "failed to update patch branch b"
a is moved and its persisted state is in_sync
b keeps the pushed tip, c is unprocessed with its previous persisted state
a rebuild job is enqueued for the moved branch a
upstream_head_sha and last_sync_at are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: r=sync(); assert r.status==500; assert r.error=='failed to update patch branch b'; assert rev(a)==forkA; assert jobs==1; assert ws.last_sync_at==before

tests.title: A moved disabled patch is refreshed and reported but does not trigger a rebuild; active and conflict ones do
given: real fork and upstream with upstream unchanged
a fast-forwardable patch with status disabled in one run, conflict in another, active in a third
tests.when: an origin-mode sync runs for each
then: the disabled run moves the ref, reports fast_forwarded and enqueues no job (rebuild_triggered false)
the conflict and active runs enqueue a rebuild job
tests.pseudocode: for st in [disabled,conflict,active]: r=sync(st); assert r.patches_synced[0].action=='fast_forwarded'; assert r.rebuild_triggered==(st!='disabled')

tests.title: For any hub-mode sync or report-policy sync no backup ref is written and no diverged branch is moved; hub mode writes no patch ref at all
given: a real repository with generated patch branches, fork branches and statuses and a recording GitRunner
tests.when: for any sync where the source is hub, or the source is origin with policy report
then: no refs/hub/replaced/* ref exists afterwards
every diverged branch keeps its old SHA
in hub mode the recorder saw zero update-ref calls
tests.pseudocode: for cfg in gen(): sync(cfg); assert refs('refs/hub/replaced/')==[]; if cfg.source=='hub': assert updateRefCalls==[]

tests.title: A patch-only change with upstream unchanged reaches merge detection on the refreshed tips
given: real fork and upstream, origin mode, upstream_head_sha equal to upstream HEAD
an active patch that fast-forwards and whose new tip is already contained in upstream
then: merge detection runs and the patch is marked merged_upstream
patches_merged lists it
with no patch change and no upstream advance, merge detection does not run
tests.pseudocode: r=sync(); assert detector.calls==1; assert r.patches_merged==['feat']; r2=sync(); assert detector.calls==1

tests.title: With the hub source merge detection runs exactly when upstream advanced
given: hub mode, a counting merge-detection stub
tests.when: one sync with upstream unchanged and one with upstream advanced
then: detection runs 0 times for the first and once for the second
tests.pseudocode: sync(unchanged); assert detect.n==0; sync(advanced); assert detect.n==1

tests.title: A patch-only change enqueues one deduplicated rebuild job with the standard key, group and submitter
given: real SQLite job queue, origin mode, upstream unchanged, a fast-forwardable active patch
a caller identity
a second scenario where a rebuild job for the slug is already queued, and a third where a newly merged patch is the only change
tests.when: a sync runs in each scenario
then: the first enqueues type rebuild with key slug, group slug:integration_branch and SubmittedBy the caller, and returns rebuild_triggered true with rebuild_job_id
the second returns rebuild_triggered false (deduplicated)
the third also enqueues a rebuild
tests.pseudocode: r=sync(); assert job.key==slug and job.group==slug+':'+integ and job.submitted_by==caller; assert r.rebuild_triggered

tests.title: AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC=false suppresses the rebuild for a patch change and for an upstream advance
given: AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC is "false"
a patch-only change in one run and an upstream advance in another
then: no job is enqueued
rebuild_triggered is false in both responses
tests.pseudocode: setVar('AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC','false'); assert sync(patchOnly).rebuild_triggered==false and jobs==0

tests.title: last_sync_at and updated_at are written on every completed sync in both modes while upstream_head_sha is written only on advance
given: a workspace with an old last_sync_at
a no-change sync in hub mode and a no-change sync in origin mode, then an upstream-advance sync
then: last_sync_at and updated_at are newer after each sync
upstream_head_sha is unchanged after the no-change syncs and updated after the advance
tests.pseudocode: for mode in [hub,origin]: sync(); assert ws.last_sync_at>old and ws.upstream_head_sha==oldSha

tests.title: A sync where nothing changed returns empty patches_merged and rebuild_triggered false
given: upstream unchanged and, in origin mode, all candidates in_sync
tests.when: a sync runs in hub and in origin mode
then: the status is 200
patches_merged is []
rebuild_triggered is false and no job is enqueued
tests.pseudocode: r=sync(); assert r.status==200 and r.patches_merged==[] and r.rebuild_triggered==false and jobs==0

tests.title: origin_fetched is always present, and a hub response gains no other field
given: hub mode response and origin mode response
tests.when: the standalone route and the workspace sync route are called
then: origin_fetched is false in hub mode and true in origin mode
the hub response key set equals the previous key set plus origin_fetched
tests.pseudocode: assert keys(hubResp)==oldKeys+['origin_fetched']; assert originResp.origin_fetched==true

tests.title: In origin mode patches_synced elements and patches_diverged follow the omission rules
given: origin mode with candidates covering created, fast_forwarded, replaced, in_sync, diverged (report) and missing_on_origin outcomes
then: each element has branch_name, action, state
local_sha is omitted for a missing local branch, origin_sha for a missing fork branch, replaced_sha unless action is replaced
patches_diverged lists exactly the diverged branches
under replace patches_diverged is []
tests.pseudocode: for e in r.patches_synced: assert ('replaced_sha' in e)==(e.action=='replaced')

tests.title: Empty patches_synced and patches_diverged serialise as [] in origin mode and are omitted in hub mode, in both body shapes
given: CarryPatchSyncResponse and the asExtras map for origin mode with zero candidates and for hub mode
then: origin mode JSON contains "patches_synced":[] and "patches_diverged":[] (not null, not omitted) in the body and in the extras
hub mode contains neither key in either form
tests.pseudocode: b=json(resp); assert b.patches_synced==[] and b.patches_diverged==[]; assert 'patches_synced' not in hub.asExtras()

tests.title: afc workspace sync prints the new fields and exits 0 even with diverged branches when the flag is absent
given: a stub hub returning a response with origin_fetched true, patches_synced and patches_diverged ["feat"] plus all existing fields
then: the exit code is 0
the printed JSON contains origin_fetched, patches_synced, patches_diverged and every existing field unchanged
tests.pseudocode: code,out=run(['workspace','sync',slug]); assert code==0; assert json(out).patches_diverged==['feat']

tests.title: --fail-on-diverged prints the JSON and a message naming the branches and exits 3 only when diverged is non-empty
given: stub hub returning patches_diverged ["a","b"] in one run and [] in another
then: the first run prints the JSON, then a message containing a and b, and exits 3
the second run exits 0
tests.pseudocode: code,out,err=run([...,'--fail-on-diverged']); assert code==3; assert 'a' in err and 'b' in err

tests.title: With --wait the diverged check runs after the wait and a wait failure takes precedence
given: stub hub returning patches_diverged ["a"] and a rebuild job id
a job-status stub that succeeds in one run and fails in another
a stub returning a request error (exit 2) in a third run
then: the wait polling happens before the exit decision
wait success gives exit 3
wait failure gives exit 1
the exit-2 case keeps its current meaning
tests.pseudocode: assert run(waitOk)==3; assert run(waitFail)==1; assert run(usageErr)==2

tests.title: The migration adds the three nullable columns to an existing patches table idempotently without backfill
given: a real database whose patches table predates this spec and holds rows
then: origin_sync_state, origin_sha and origin_synced_at exist as nullable columns
existing rows have NULL in all three
no run returns an error
tests.pseudocode: for i in 1..3: assert initSchema(db)==nil; cols=pragma(patches); assert {'origin_sync_state','origin_sha','origin_synced_at'}<=cols; assert allNull(rows)

tests.title: Origin mode persists state, fork SHA and an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp per candidate and clears merged and deleted rows
given: real database, origin mode, candidates in states in_sync, diverged (report) and missing_on_origin
a merged_upstream row and a deleted row carrying stale origin columns
then: each candidate row has the matching origin_sync_state, origin_sha (NULL for missing_on_origin) and a timestamp parsable by apikit.ParseUTC
the merged_upstream and deleted rows have all three columns NULL
tests.pseudocode: rows=select(patches); assert row(missing).origin_sha is NULL; assert parseUTC(row.origin_synced_at) ok; assert row(merged).origin_sync_state is NULL

tests.title: A hub-mode sync clears origin columns of every patch row of the workspace only
given: patch rows of the workspace with all statuses carrying origin state
a row of another workspace with origin state
then: all rows of the synced workspace have the three columns NULL
the other workspace's row is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: sync(hub); assert all(r.origin_sync_state is NULL for r in rows(slug)); assert other.origin_sync_state=='diverged'

tests.title: PatchStore gains write and clear methods on SQLPatchStore and the doubles without changing existing methods
given: an SQLPatchStore on a test database and the in-memory test double
tests.when: the new write method is called for a patch and the clear methods are called for one row and for a whole workspace
then: the three columns are set, then cleared, in both implementations
existing PatchStore methods keep their signatures and results (the interface is still satisfied by existing callers)
tests.pseudocode: store.SetOriginSyncState(id,'in_sync',sha,ts); assert get(id).origin_sha==sha; store.ClearOriginSyncState(slug); assert get(id).origin_sha is NULL

tests.title: Every workspace patch REST response exposes the three fields and omits them when null
given: a patch with origin state and a patch without
tests.when: list, get, create and update patch endpoints are called
then: the patch with state shows origin_sync_state, origin_sha and origin_synced_at
the other patch's JSON contains none of the three keys
the existing fields are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: r=GET /workspaces/s/patches; assert 'origin_sha' in r[0] and 'origin_sha' not in r[1]

tests.title: patch-status shows per-patch origin fields and summary counts, with counts 0 in hub mode
given: patches with origin_sync_state diverged, missing_on_origin, in_sync and null
a second workspace in hub mode
then: each patch carries the three fields, omitted when null
the summary has patches_diverged 1 and patches_missing_on_origin 1 for the origin workspace
the hub workspace summary has both counts present and equal to 0
tests.pseudocode: r=GET patch-status; assert r.summary.patches_diverged==1; assert hub.summary.patches_missing_on_origin==0

tests.title: A mixed origin-mode sync emits one hub.patch.sync event with the branch lists and the standard actor, resource and slug
given: a recording audit emitter, origin mode, candidates covering created, fast_forwarded, replaced, diverged (second run under report) and missing_on_origin
a caller credential
then: exactly one hub.patch.sync event is emitted using the constant from internal/audit/types.go
metadata has origin_fetched true and created, fast_forwarded, replaced, diverged, missing_on_origin lists of branch names
actor is the caller, resource_type is patch and the workspace slug is set
tests.pseudocode: ev=emitter.byType(EventPatchSync); assert len(ev)==1; assert ev[0].metadata.replaced==['r']; assert ev[0].actor==caller and ev[0].resource_type=='patch'

tests.title: Each replaced branch emits a hub.patch.replace event and an info log with slug, branch and both SHAs
given: a recording emitter and a captured logger
two diverged candidates under replace
then: two hub.patch.replace events are emitted with branch_name, replaced_sha and origin_sha
the actor, resource_type patch and slug are set as for the sync event
two info log lines carry slug, branch and both SHAs
tests.pseudocode: evs=emitter.byType(EventPatchReplace); assert len(evs)==2; assert evs[0].metadata.replaced_sha==oldTip

tests.title: Hub mode emits no hub.patch.sync event
given: hub mode with a recording emitter
tests.when: a sync completes, with and without upstream change
then: no hub.patch.sync and no hub.patch.replace event is emitted
tests.pseudocode: sync(); assert emitter.byType(EventPatchSync)==[]

tests.title: A ref-write failure still emits events for the outcomes already produced
given: recording emitter, a first candidate replaced and a second candidate whose compare-and-swap fails
then: one hub.patch.sync event lists the first branch under replaced and omits the failed and unprocessed ones
one hub.patch.replace event is emitted for the first branch
tests.pseudocode: r=sync(); assert r.status==500; assert emitter.byType(EventPatchSync)[0].metadata.replaced==['a']

tests.title: A nil audit emitter skips emission and the sync completes
given: SyncAPIConfig.Audit is nil, origin mode with a replaced branch
then: the status is 200 with the normal body and no panic
tests.pseudocode: cfg.Audit=nil; r=sync(); assert r.status==200 and r.patches_synced[0].action=='replaced'

tests.title: A failing emitter is logged and does not change the response
given: an emitter whose Emit returns an error, a second sync with a succeeding emitter on an identical fixture
then: the status and body are identical in both runs
the error is logged
tests.pseudocode: assert sync(failing).status==sync(ok).status and body equal; assert log.contains(err)

tests.title: docs/api.md documents the new sync behaviour, variables, fields, messages and events
given: the repository docs/api.md
tests.when: a docs test reads the file
then: it mentions origin_fetched, patches_synced, patches_diverged, PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE, PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY, origin_sync_state, origin_sha, origin_synced_at, patches_missing_on_origin
it contains the strings "origin fetch failed", "failed to resolve origin credentials", hub.patch.sync and hub.patch.replace
the AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC text mentions patch changes
tests.pseudocode: for s in required: assert s in read('docs/api.md')

tests.title: docs/openapi.yaml describes the sync response, patch and patch-status changes and stays valid YAML
given: the repository docs/openapi.yaml
then: CarryPatchSyncResponse has origin_fetched in its required list and optional patches_synced and patches_diverged
the sync operation has 502 and 200 responses covering origin failures
the patch and patch-status schemas contain the three origin fields and the two summary counts

tests.title: docs/cli.md and docs/carry_patch_workflow.md document the flag, exit code and variables, and docs/configuration.md is unchanged
given: the repository docs files and the git diff of the change
then: docs/cli.md mentions --fail-on-diverged and exit code 3
docs/carry_patch_workflow.md mentions PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE, PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY and fork_push_control
docs/configuration.md does not mention PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE
tests.pseudocode: assert '--fail-on-diverged' in read('docs/cli.md'); assert 'PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE' not in read('docs/configuration.md')

tests.title: A fork-side fix fast-forwards a patch and triggers a rebuild with upstream unchanged
given: running hub handlers with a real fork, real upstream, real trunk, real SQLite database and job queue
PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin, upstream unchanged, an active patch behind the fork's tip
then: refs/heads/<branch> equals the fork tip
patches_synced has action fast_forwarded, origin_fetched true, rebuild_triggered true with a rebuild_job_id
the patch row has origin_sync_state in_sync, origin_sha and origin_synced_at
last_sync_at is updated and upstream_head_sha unchanged
a hub.patch.sync event is recorded and a rebuild job is queued
real_components: git runner and real git repositories

tests.title: Divergence under replace keeps a backup of the discarded tip and enqueues a rebuild
given: running hub handlers with real fork, upstream, trunk, database and queue
origin mode, policy unset, a patch whose hub tip was pushed and diverged from the fork
then: refs/hub/replaced/<branch> holds the old hub tip
refs/heads/<branch> holds the fork tip
the response has action replaced with replaced_sha and patches_diverged []
hub.patch.replace and hub.patch.sync events are recorded and a rebuild job is queued
real_components: git runner and real git repositories

tests.title: A CI sync with --fail-on-diverged under report exits 3 and the dashboard shows the divergence
given: a running hub with real repositories and database, origin mode, PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY=report, a diverged patch
the real afc CLI pointed at the hub
tests.when: afc workspace sync --fail-on-diverged is run, then GET /workspaces/:slug/patch-status is called
then: the CLI prints the response JSON and a message naming the branch and exits 3
the local branch is unchanged
patch-status shows origin_sync_state diverged for the patch and patches_diverged 1 in the summary
real_components: git runner and real git repositories

tests.title: An unreachable fork aborts the sync with 502 origin_fetch_failed and changes nothing
given: a running hub with real upstream and trunk, origin remote pointing at a non-existent path
origin mode, upstream advanced, snapshot of workspace row, patch rows and refs/heads/*
then: the status is 502 with message "origin fetch failed" and error_type origin_fetch_failed
upstream_head_sha, last_sync_at, patch statuses, origin sync columns and refs/heads/* equal the snapshot
no rebuild job is queued
real_components: git runner and real git repositories

tests.title: A hub-mode sync with no upstream change only refreshes last_sync_at and returns origin_fetched false
given: a running hub with real repositories and database, PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE unset, no upstream change
patch rows carrying stale origin columns, counting stubs on the origin fetch and origin credential resolver wired in the config
then: the origin fetch and credential stubs are called 0 times
no patch ref is written
last_sync_at is updated and all origin columns are cleared
the response has empty patches_merged, rebuild_triggered false, origin_fetched false and no patches_synced field
real_components: git runner and real git repositories

tests.title: A lost compare-and-swap keeps the earlier outcome, still enqueues the rebuild and returns 500
given: a running hub with real fork, upstream, trunk, database and queue, origin mode, two fast-forwardable candidates
a hub push to the second branch lands after its ancestry check
then: the status is 500 with message "failed to update patch branch <second>"
the first branch is moved and persisted in_sync
the second branch holds the pushed tip
a rebuild job is queued
hub.patch.sync lists the first branch under fast_forwarded
upstream_head_sha and last_sync_at are unchanged
real_components: git runner and real git repositories
